paragraphs: His family is put with the villages of the St. Joseph, on the St. Joseph River, east round the lake (three or four villages in May 1812), one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.
He is of the Sturgeon gens (N′-mă′), and his children are of it after him.
In lodge no. 1 he lives with his wife Prairie Eagle Shadow Woman, his son Little Sturgeon (9), his son Little Fish (4) and his daughter Young Little Fish (15).
In the spring he helped at the sugar camp, and in summer fished the river and the lake while the corn grew at the village.
He came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.
